title: Charles Leclerc #16
description: High-octane Formula 1 showcase with canvas telemetry visualizers and fluid kinetic transitions.

featuredSlide.aboutP1: Motorsport fans love granular telemetry: throttle curves and sector deltas. I wanted to translate the sensory velocity of Formula 1 into an interactive web experience powered by kinetic motion and sound.
featuredSlide.aboutP2: I engineered an interactive Canvas 2D tachometer revving dynamically with scroll speed, custom redline shaders, video scrub triggers, and sector delta timelines comparing telemetry across Monaco and Monza.

caseStudy.tagline: High-octane Formula 1 showcase with canvas telemetry visualizers and fluid kinetic transitions.

problem.headline: Translating the sensory velocity and telemetry of Formula 1 into interactive web form.
problem.description: Motorsport enthusiasts love granular telemetry: throttle traces, braking curves, and sector deltas. This project explores high-impact sports storytelling using typography, audio cues, and telemetry charts.

architecture.headline: Canvas-driven RPM tachometer and kinetic scrub animations.
architecture.description: Engineered an interactive tachometer dial that revs based on user scroll velocity, paired with smooth video scrub triggers.

highlights.title: Velocity-Driven UI Feedback
highlights.detail: Scroll velocity feeds directly into tachometer needle position with spring physics.

highlights.title: Dynamic Redline Shader
highlights.detail: Glow filters simulating race steering wheel shift indicator LEDs.

features.title: Interactive F1 Tachometer
features.description: Dynamic RPM gauge reacting to scroll speed with redline sound triggers.

features.title: Sector Delta Timeline
features.description: Qualifying lap breakdown comparing telemetry across Monaco and Monza.

takeaways: Tying scroll velocity to mechanical feedback creates an immediate physical connection between user input and visual response.
